races.name: Kauto The King Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hercule Du Seuil
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with class advantage but struggling for current yard, 27 days since last run could be ideal preparation
runners_data.comment: Grade 3 winner (2m4f) for Willie Mullins last year but offered little as yet for new yard.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make an impact in three starts for this yard this year, but he showed some smart form in Ireland for Willie Mullins, notably landing a 2m4f Grade 3 at around this time last season; looks attractively treated on that evidence; one to watch in the market, though a return to form is needed.

runners_data.name: Etalon
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in career-best form with cheekpieces fitted, 74-day break may have freshened him up perfectly
runners_data.comment: Ascot win and good third since the cheekpieces went on; below par latest but respected.
runners_data.spotlight: Fitting of cheekpieces sparked a revival in December, when landing a fifth success over fences at Ascot (2m3f, good to soft); followed that up with a career-best RPR when third off this mark there (2m5f) the following month; respected but he'll need to leave behind a lesser effort last time.

runners_data.name: Light N Strike
runners_data.note: Won this race off same mark last year but struggling since switching yards, hold-up style suits race shape
runners_data.comment: Won this off today's mark last year but form for this stable has been poor.
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive for Emma Lavelle last term, winning this off today's mark and backing it up with solid placed efforts; however, he's struggled for this yard (early unseat in Kerry National, pulled up at Chepstow and tailed off at Cheltenham when last seen in October) and now has something to prove.

runners_data.name: Centara
runners_data.note: Uncontested leader who thrives at this track on good to soft ground, 194 days off could be concern or benefit
runners_data.comment: Five chase wins last summer; second wind op; steps up in trip but needs to find more.
runners_data.spotlight: Highly progressive over fences last summer, winning five handicaps (four here) at around 2m on ground no worse than good to soft, though he ended the campaign pulled up at Cheltenham; has since had a second wind op and could find more at this longer trip (2m3f hurdle winner), which will be needed off this mark following a break.

runners_data.name: Western General
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner with current form, career-best RPRs suggest he's peaking at right time
runners_data.comment: Back to form post wind op; up in trip but respected judged on recent good form.
runners_data.spotlight: Back to form after a second wind op, posting career-best RPRs when scoring at Chepstow in February and when runner-up at Hereford the following month (both at 2m); has his best form over shorter but shapes as though this trip should suit and he commands respect on that recent form.

runners_data.name: Ventura Highway
runners_data.note: Prominent style but unclear current ability, ex-French performer needs to prove himself in this grade
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; Auteuil winner last May; below par since; bit to prove on UK debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French; gained a chase success at Auteuil (2m6f) last May but hasn't matched that since; current ability is a little tricky to pin down and he looks to have something to find on RPRs on this British debut.

runners_data.name: Somespring Special
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won at Chepstow but hit with 7lb rise, recent form suggests she's struggling with new mark
runners_data.comment: 4-15 over fences; below par twice this year; only 2lb lower and has something to prove.
runners_data.spotlight: 4-15 over fences; gained a win at Chepstow (extended 2m3f, good) in October but hit with a 7lb rise and she's been well held on both outings this year, most recently trailing home last of three at Wincanton (2m, good) three weeks ago; only 2lb lower and now has plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Centara is the only confirmed front runner and will set the pace from flag to finish without pressure early on. Western General may provide some company from the prominent position, but this shapes as a controlled tempo through the first circuit. The lack of natural early speed means Centara can dictate terms and potentially steal a march turning for home. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses like Hercule Du Seuil, Etalon, and Light N Strike who can benefit from the sustainable pace and time their challenges late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Centara sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays manageable throughout
scenarios.body: The patient riders can time their runs perfectly as Centara weakens, with the class horses sweeping past in the final furlong. This controlled tempo allows the higher-rated hold-up performers to showcase their superior ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Centara Stays Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly pedestrian and no one challenges the leader early enough
scenarios.body: Centara gets such an easy lead that he builds an unassailable advantage, staying on strongly up the home straight. His previous success record at this track under similar conditions proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Western General or Ventura Highway press Centara earlier than expected creating a moderate pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo puts pressure on the leader while still being within range for the prominent runners to strike. This mid-race pressure sets up perfectly for those tracking just off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a crawl with no one willing to commit until very late
scenarios.body: The race turns into a sprint from the final fence with positioning becoming crucial rather than stamina. Fresh legs and recent form become more important than class in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Centara gets too easy a lead early and builds an unassailable advantage before anyone reacts
Western General fails to provide any pressure on Centara, making the pace even more sedate than expected
Hercule Du Seuil shows ring rustiness after 27 days off, suggesting the long break hasn't helped
Etalon travels strongly through the race suggesting his 74-day break has worked perfectly
Light N Strike gets a clean run through to show if the track and conditions can spark a revival

races.name: Racing To School Reaches 25 Years Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bold Step
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for in-form Henderson stable, handles soft ground well, 117 days off but classy operator

runners_data.name: Outmaster
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity from Nicholls yard, lightly raced with 388 days absence creating uncertainty

runners_data.name: River Don
runners_data.note: Point winner last time, amateur jockey a concern, cheekpieces applied for stable debut
runners_data.comment: Off mark at seventh attempt in points last month; cheekpieces on for rules/hurdle debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the seventh attempt in points when winning a three-finisher maiden at Cothelstone (3m, good to soft) last month for this stable; cheekpieces go on for rules/hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Jubertilee
runners_data.note: Faded badly on rules debut at Chepstow, drop to 2m likely too sharp for this stayer
runners_data.comment: 6-21 in points; well held Chepstow debut over 2m but this longer trip will suit.
runners_data.spotlight: 6-21 in points and in good heart this year, but never sighted when well held on hurdle/rules debut at Chepstow last month, possibly finding the drop to 2m counting against him; should be better suited by this stamina test but still likely to find a few too good.

runners_data.name: Name Me Nicely
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid soft ground record, 47 days off ideal for Bailey/Nicholls partnership

runners_data.name: At Sunrise
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader, 147 days off but gets valuable weight allowance, must dictate from front

runners_data.name: Lirone Du Seuil
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from strong Skelton yard, French winner on very soft but disappointed in Britain
runners_data.comment: Bit to prove returning from a break, but tongue-tie added and remains in excellent hands.
runners_data.spotlight: French 2m2f hurdle winner on very soft who folded tamely at Wetherby (2m, soft; 14-1) on British debut, and fared little better when a remote fourth at Plumpton (2m4f, soft) in January; has a bit to prove returning from a break but now goes in a tongue-tie and remains in excellent hands.

runners_data.name: Alberts Bay
runners_data.note: Front runner returning from 573-day absence, rusty last time and major fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 9yo; career hit by absences; back after another break on this stable debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Third on hurdle debut over C&D in September 2023 after a long absence, but off again afterwards and last of seven in October 2024; returns from another lengthy layoff on stable debut.

runners_data.name: Double Tiger
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good form for Greatrex, solid recent efforts and handles conditions

runners_data.name: Style De Folie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with cheekpieces fitted, well beaten in recent hurdle attempts over shorter
runners_data.comment: Well held in both hurdle starts (2m3f); cheekpieces latest; up in trip but hard to fancy.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 53l and 31l in his two hurdle races (2m3f), with cheekpieces latest; up in trip but difficult to make a case for.

races.paceDynamic: At Sunrise and Alberts Bay will engage from the front with both confirmed leaders needing to dictate from flag fall. At Sunrise brings fresher prospects after 147 days off while Alberts Bay returns from 573 days away and looked rusty last time out. With only two genuine pace angles, they'll likely go steady early before quickening from three out, creating a searching test in testing ground. This moderate early pace followed by late acceleration strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders go steady early and the pace quickens late.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop allows closers to get into contention before unleashing finishing kicks up the testing hill. Name Me Nicely and Style De Folie benefit most from patient rides and strong finishes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Battle Hard
scenarios.trigger: If At Sunrise and Alberts Bay engage in a prolonged speed duel.
scenarios.body: Their honest gallop creates genuine pace that suits prominent racers who can track and pounce. Bold Step and Double Tiger can sit close enough to capitalize when the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Maiden Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the form horses fail to handle conditions or distance.
scenarios.body: The testing ground and extended trip catches out several fancied runners allowing a bigger-priced maiden to strike. River Don or Outmaster could benefit from their point-to-point experience in these conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders show rustiness and go too slow early.
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace creates a messy sprint finish where anything can happen. The race becomes a lottery with prominent runners getting first run on tired leaders.

watchPoints.text: Alberts Bay may not be fit enough after 573 days off and could compound front-running concerns
River Don's amateur jockey Mr Charlie Marshall may struggle with tactical demands in competitive field
At Sunrise carries the pace burden alone if Alberts Bay shows rustiness early
Name Me Nicely's hold-up style perfectly suits if the leaders engage in honest gallop
Bold Step represents powerful Henderson/Bowen combination dropping back from chasing

races.name: No Drama This End Club Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Elysian Knight
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent hurdles form but winless over fences this term, 17 days since last run ideal for Sean Bowen
runners_data.comment: Yet to win over fences or in handicap company but needs respect dropped into a class 4.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 over fences this term but far from disgraced on a couple of starts and ran respectably when fourth back over hurdles at Plumpton (3m1f, good) last month; yet to win in handicap company but drops in class returned to fences and warrants respect.

runners_data.name: Storminhome
runners_data.note: Pressing style suits, showed renewed vigor in blinkers last time at Southwell, 65-day break could be freshening
runners_data.comment: Back to form in blinkers latest and likely to play a leading role if headgear works again.
runners_data.spotlight: Suffered a couple of heavy defeats after a long absence but then went very close to a first chase win in first-time blinkers at Southwell (3m, soft) last time, with the winner running well since; remains on a competitive mark and is one to consider if the headgear continues to have a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Astronomic View
runners_data.note: Prominent style with good going record, lightest weight at 156lbs gives tactical advantage, 50-day gap not concerning

runners_data.name: Rickety Bridge
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls runner with prominent style, form patchy but showed revival signs last time, 32 days ideal spacing
runners_data.comment: Signs of a revival last time and he could be suited by switch to fences.
runners_data.spotlight: Landed a Southwell maiden hurdle (2m4f, soft) in March 2024; largely out of form in limited starts since but there were signs of a revival here (3m2f, good) last month in first-time cheekpieces; needs to back that up but could improve for this switch to fences.

runners_data.name: Dyno Dave
runners_data.note: Henderson-trained with prominent tendencies, lightest of the big names at 154lbs, 29-day gap keeps him sharp

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners showing prominent/pressing styles and no confirmed front-runner, this becomes a tactical battle for early position. Elysian Knight and Storminhome are most likely to dispute the early lead, with the others tracking close behind in what will be a bunched field. The lack of a true pace angle means they'll likely go steady early before quickening from the home turn. This measured pace setup strongly favours horses with tactical speed and finishing kick over pure stamina plodders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady with multiple horses in contention turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early burn-up means this becomes about who has the most left in the tank for the final climb. Horses with recent form and lighter weights get the edge in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Elysian Knight or Storminhome gets an uncontested lead and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: They can dictate fractions and kick clear when the pressure comes, making it hard for the others to peg them back up the hill. The leader's stamina reserves prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If they go too steady early and it becomes a mad dash from two out
scenarios.body: The race turns into a pure speed test where class and recent race fitness matter most. Horses carrying less weight can quicken better in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If genuine early pace develops with multiple horses vying for the lead
scenarios.body: The strong gallop stretches the field and makes it a true staying test where only the most genuine stayers survive. Experience over this trip becomes crucial.

watchPoints.text: Storminhome could prove hard to pass if Harry Skelton gets him into an early rhythm and those blinkers continue to work
Elysian Knight's jumping under pressure given his winless record over fences this season could be exposed if challenged hard
The going change from good to soft could catch out any horse not fully tuned up after their respective layoffs
Astronomic View's weight advantage at 156lbs becomes more significant if this turns into a tactical sprint finish
Dyno Dave's recent Plumpton win over fences suggests Henderson has found the key to this enigmatic performer

races.name: Welcoming Newton Abbot Business Club Members Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Northern Air
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage with 32 days off and relying on others to set it up properly for his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: First Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner perfectly positioned to track Gower Prince, though 50-day absence raises fitness questions despite solid soft ground record.

runners_data.name: Cobbler's Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent poor form suggests he's struggling to recapture his hurdles ability over fences, wrong running style for this pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Good-ground hurdle winner; yet to win over fences but latest fourth was encouraging.
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground 2m maiden hurdle winner a year ago and he's looked a work in progress since switching to fences last season; latest 5l fourth at Ascot (2m1f, good) returned to better ground was encouraging though and he's come a long way down the weights; needs to build on that and not of of this if doing so.

runners_data.name: Lightning Flash
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits this race shape but 54-day layoff and previous falling tendency over fences creates reliability concerns.
runners_data.comment: Won chase debut at Chepstow but out of form since falling at Ludlow in November.
runners_data.spotlight: Made a winning start over fences at Chepstow (2m) in October and looked set for a second success when falling two out at Ludlow (2m) the following month; however, well held in his two runs since, with his jumping far from fluent when last of three at Doncaster in March after a break; now has something to prove.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner whose recent Market Rasen second suggests return to form, hood back on and perfectly suited to dictate this tactical affair.
runners_data.comment: Back to near best when second on stable debut last time and strong claims if repeating it.
runners_data.spotlight: Back to near best on first start for this stable when runner-up at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) with the hood back on; remains well treated on past form after 3lb rise and holds strong claims if able to repeat the effort.

races.paceDynamic: Gower Prince will dictate proceedings from the front with no genuine pace rival to apply pressure, allowing him to bowl along at a comfortable gallop over this extended 2m½f trip. First Angel and Lightning Flash will track prominently behind the leader, while Northern Air and Cobbler's Boy will settle further back looking to mount late challenges. With only one confirmed front-runner and a manageable field size, this sets up as a tactical affair where the pace will be steady rather than punishing. This race shape clearly favours the prominent runners who can track Gower Prince closely and have first run on the hold-up horses when the pace inevitably quickens approaching the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If First Angel or Lightning Flash can track Gower Prince closely without being headed off at the front
scenarios.body: The manageable pace allows them to conserve energy while staying in touch, then use their class to sweep past a tiring leader. Their prominent running styles are perfectly suited to this tactical setup where positioning behind the lone leader becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince maintains his advantage and kicks again when challenged turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure means he travels well within himself, then his recent Market Rasen runner-up effort suggests he has the class to see off late challengers. His hold-up rivals face a difficult task trying to reel in a horse who's had an easy lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Air or Cobbler's Boy can overcome the pace disadvantage with superior finishing kicks
scenarios.body: The tactical pace gives them a chance to close despite their running styles being poorly suited to this race shape. However, they'll need the front-runners to completely fold for this to work.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince goes too fast early or the prominent horses fail to track him properly
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble where any horse with energy left can capitalize, though this seems unlikely given the field composition. This chaotic finish would need multiple tactical errors from the obvious contenders.

watchPoints.text: Lightning Flash has fallen twice over fences in recent runs, creating serious reliability concerns despite his prominent tactical advantage.
Gower Prince's trainer Jonjo O'Neill is 0/19 in the last 14 days, suggesting stable may be out of form despite horse's individual promise.
Northern Air faces a 32-day absence which could blunt his finishing kick when needing maximum sharpness to overcome tactical disadvantage.
First Angel's 50-day break is the longest among the field, monitor for any signs of rustiness in the preliminaries.
Cobbler's Boy has failed to place in his last five starts, watch for any early signs of confidence returning over his fences.

races.name: Par Inn Celebrating 50 Next Year Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ghost Dancing
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who suits the likely strong pace, 54 days off but Alan King 3/21 in last 14 days raises concern

runners_data.name: Belle Le Grand
runners_data.note: Natural leader with stamina proven at trip, but 0 wins from 12 handicap attempts suggests she finds one too good
runners_data.comment: 0-5 in handicaps but she's on a reduced mark and could be dangerous with cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: Won two novice hurdles on good ground last May (2m/2m1f); no impact at 12-1 or bigger in five handicaps but she rallied to finish a respectable sixth of 15 at Kelso (2m, good to soft) in March; continues to drop down the weights and could be dangerous if first-time cheekpieces work.

runners_data.name: Future Bucks
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter but was pulled up on British handicap debut and looks vulnerable off this mark
runners_data.comment: Pulled up on handicap debut at Newbury in March and needs a major revival back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French 5yo who won British debut at Windsor (2m, good to soft) in November but she's been disappointing since and was pulled on handicap debut at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft; 66-1) in March; that was a tough assignment but she needs a major revival on this drop back in trip.

runners_data.name: Riviera Walk
runners_data.note: Front-runner who won impressively but pulled up last time, inexperienced 5lb claimer a worry in competitive heat
runners_data.comment: Easy winner of a Catterick maiden but was pulled up on her handicap debut last time
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper scorer who won by 15l in a Catterick maiden (1m7f, good) in March but she was pulled up on her handicap debut at Kelso (2m, good to soft) last time; still has low mileage but she's not been easy to predict and needs to bounce back again.

runners_data.name: Best Night
runners_data.note: Course winner who can track the pace, only 14 days since last run keeps her sharp but has regressed recently
runners_data.comment: Won at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March but she's taken two backward steps since
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on good and soft ground; C&D winner who scored at Huntingdon (2m) in March but she's taken backward steps in her two subsequent runs; only 2lb higher than for her last win but she needs to rediscover her spark.

runners_data.name: Babychino
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with 39 days off, carries just 142lbs but needs everything to fall right from the back
runners_data.comment: Third on handicap debut at Uttoxeter but she's 5lb out of the weights here; has work to do
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; came from long way back to finish third on handicap debut at Uttoxeter (2m, good to soft; 50-1) in March but she was beaten 11l and this is tougher from 5lb out of the weights; has work to do.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Prominent early but fades in finish, breeding suggests trip will suit but poor recent form concerning
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 6yo and she's a possible improver on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to three hurdle winners including the smart Polly Peachum (2m-2m6f); well held at big prices in both completed starts over hurdles but she's had only four runs and it wouldn't be a surprise if she showed a lot more on this handicap debut; needs a close look in the market.

runners_data.name: Reel Orange
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who won here last time with cheekpieces, proven course form gives her solid claims
runners_data.comment: Made the breakthrough over C&D last month and she's a big player again off 3lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the ninth attempt over hurdles when justifying favouritism in a C&D handicap (good; cheekpieces added) last month; there wasn't much separating the first four but a 3lb rise looks fair and her confidence should be boosted after that success; big player again in her bid to make it 2-4 for Joe Tizzard.

races.paceDynamic: Riviera Walk, Belle Le Grand, and Future Bucks will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with all three capable of taking it on early. The pace will be honest throughout the 2m1f trip on this good to soft ground, creating a stamina test rather than a sprint finish. With three confirmed front-runners in a small field, the leaders will go hard and potentially set it up for those tracking just behind or held up with finishing kick. This sustained pace favours prominent trackers and hold-up horses who can stay the trip and have a turn of foot when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders go too hard early and fade from 2f out
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop will find out the front-runners as they've all shown vulnerability in recent handicaps. Horses tracking in behind like Ghost Dancing and Best Night can pick up the pieces with their class edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders gets soft splits and dictates more sensibly
scenarios.body: Belle Le Grand or Riviera Walk could get first run on their rivals if they can shake off the other pace-setters. Their proven stamina at this trip gives them the edge if they get tactical breathing space.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce and collapses dramatically in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Babychino and Reel Orange come from furthest back and could have the most petrol left when others empty out. Both have shown they can make up significant ground when things fall their way.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Dancing or Best Night get perfect positions just off the pace
scenarios.body: These higher-rated mares can use their class advantage from ideal stalking positions. Best Night's course winner credentials and Ghost Dancing's trainer form give them the tactical edge.

watchPoints.text: Riviera Walk's inexperienced 5lb claimer Benjamin Macey could get outpaced or make tactical errors in this company
Future Bucks was pulled up on handicap debut and another poor show would confirm she's not cut out for British handicaps
Best Night's recent backward steps need monitoring as she's dropped to a handy mark but form is heading wrong way
The three leaders Riviera Walk, Belle Le Grand and Future Bucks could set a suicidal pace that sets up the race for closers
Ghost Dancing returns after 54 days off and needs to show the break hasn't dulled her edge from this prominent position

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who stays well but may find this tactical tempo doesn't suit his rhythm
runners_data.comment: Reliable type who was a good second when upped to 3m2f at Stratford last time; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Reliable type who has finished runner-up at Fontwell (2m1f, good) and Stratford (3m2f, good) this spring; that was his first run beyond 2m5f last time but he stayed on well and is respected off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Striking A Pose
runners_data.note: Will control the pace from the front but vulnerable if hold-up horses time their runs perfectly
runners_data.comment: Six-time hurdle winner who made all over C&D last month; big player again back up 4lb
runners_data.spotlight: Recorded his sixth hurdle win when making all off a reduced mark over C&D (good; 4-1) three weeks ago; back up 4lb but remains well treated on old form and is versatile ground-wise; key player.

runners_data.name: Baltray
runners_data.note: Prominent style but poor recent form suggests he's lost his way completely
runners_data.comment: Has struggled in his last two starts and has stamina to prove at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up off 3lb higher at Stratford (2m6f, good) in October but he's struggled in both subsequent runs; hurdling record is now 1-10 and he has stamina to prove at this new trip after another break; down the list.

runners_data.name: Mister Barclay
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer returning from 178-day break with strong soft ground record

runners_data.name: Supreme Yeats
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good hands with Skelton team but showing declining form this season
runners_data.comment: On dangerous mark but he's been out of sorts this year and losing run is mounting up
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped on his Uttoxeter win (3m, good) last July but he's 0-9 since and has been out of sorts this year; has something to prove and he was pulled up in only go at this sort of trip; cheekpieces (last used in October) are reapplied.

runners_data.name: Alan Bresil
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needs the race to develop into a genuine staying test

runners_data.name: Despereaux
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven stamina at this trip but has struggled in recent outings
runners_data.comment: Won at Hereford (3m2f) in December and has claims if he can get back near that level
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner who ended last year with a brave success at Hereford (3m2f, good to soft); well held there in both runs this spring but he got involved in a battle up front last time; a player if he can get back near his best.

runners_data.name: Sam's Amour
runners_data.note: Prominent style but form has deteriorated badly since early 2024 success
runners_data.comment: Has struggled in last five starts, including over C&D on her penultimate run; opposable
runners_data.spotlight: Triple hurdle winner (2m2f-2m5f) in 2024 but she's struggled in last five starts, including over C&D last month on her penultimate run; has plenty to prove and needs a major revival.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran in snatches last time and needs to settle better
runners_data.comment: His last win was in July 2024 and he's struggled in both runs this year; lots to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Conditions are no problem but he's not won since July 2024 and has struggled in both runs this year, including on stable debut at Ffos Las (ran in snatches) last month; has plenty to prove and needs to get back on track.

races.paceDynamic: Striking A Pose is the sole confirmed front runner and will make all the running at a controlled gallop over this stamina test. The prominent runners Juggernaut, Despereaux and Sam's Amour will track him in the early stages but none are aggressive pace-pressers. With minimal early pace pressure, this sets up as a tactical affair that will develop into a staying test from the final mile. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finish, as the lack of early pace will leave plenty in reserve for those coming from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays modest and the race becomes a sprint finish from the last half-mile
scenarios.body: The backmarkers will have too much finishing speed for the early leaders who've been given an easy time in front. Mister Barclay and Supreme Yeats are perfectly positioned to unleash late runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Running Success
scenarios.trigger: If Striking A Pose maintains his stamina advantage and no serious challengers emerge
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to dictate throughout and use his proven course form to hold off late challengers. His recent C&D win confirms he handles these exact conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can stay close enough to Striking A Pose and outstay the hold-up horses
scenarios.body: Juggernaut or Despereaux will benefit from tracking the pace without getting involved in early battles. Their superior recent form gives them the edge in a tactical finish over this extended trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Striking A Pose goes too slowly early and gets swamped by multiple finishers
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy scramble where any horse with a bit of pace can win. The form book goes out the window in a slowly-run staying test that favours whoever kicks first.

watchPoints.text: Striking A Pose could get an uncontested lead if the prominent runners don't track him closely enough early
Mister Barclay returning from a long break could need the run despite his obvious class advantage
Supreme Yeats has been out of sorts but the Skelton team are hitting form with 9 from 26 recently
The pace could collapse completely with only one genuine front runner in the field
Juggernaut may struggle tactically if this becomes too much of a sprint finish from the back
